question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence.**

Let us know what you think __in black and white.__
solution:
The correct answer is** 'in writing'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom** 'In black** **and white'** is **'In writing'.**
 
• The idiom** "in black and white"** means **something that is presented or expressed in written or printed form, and is clear, unambiguous, and definitive**. (कुछ ऐसा जो लिखित या मुद्रित रूप में प्रस्तुत या व्यक्त किया गया हो, और स्पष्ट, असंदिग्ध और निश्चित हो)
 
 
• *Example sentence: The contract clearly states the terms of the agreement** in black and white.***

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *in writing.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin**:

 
 
• This **idiom** has its roots in the world of printing. In the early days of printing, text was printed in black ink on white paper, which was considered to be a clear and **unambiguous** form of communication.
 
• This phrase was first recorded in English in the 1530s and was used to describe legal documents that were written in clear, precise language.
 
• Over time, the phrase came to be used more generally to refer to any kind of** written or printed document that is clear and definitive. **
